result.title: Compression of Vision Foundation Models for Retinal OCT via Growing-Neural-Gas Codebooks and Graph-Guided Masked Image Modeling
result.comment: 31 pages, 2 figures, 8 tables; supplementary material provided as an ancillary file
result.summary: Vision foundation models for retinal imaging are large and computationally demanding, limiting point-of-care deployment. We ask how much of such a model's downstream utility survives compression into a smaller network. We propose a topology-aware discretization framework that distills a continuous foundation model into a discrete codebook, then uses it as the reconstruction target for masked image modeling (MIM). It combines gradient-free codebook learning via Growing Neural Gas, which yields an adjacency graph over the codes, with a graph-distance soft cross-entropy loss that replaces one-hot MIM targets with topologically graded supervision. With student pretraining on 383 public Duke iAMD optical coherence tomography (OCT) volumes, the pipeline distills an 86M-parameter teacher into a 22M-parameter student with at least 3.6x fewer FLOPs. The student performs close to, and in some settings above, its teacher across three classification and two segmentation benchmarks, with the magnitude and direction of the difference depending on the teacher, task, metric, and student capacity. On the external OLIVES benchmark, it surpasses its MIRAGE teacher on every metric (98.06% vs. 95.22% balanced accuracy). It works with two Vision Transformer (ViT-Base) teachers, retinal (MIRAGE) and natural-image (DINOv3); with the out-of-domain teacher, the student outperforms it on retinal-layer segmentation, indicating that the added value of retina-specific pretraining is task-dependent: largest for segmentation, while a general-domain teacher is competitive for classification. These results yield compact retinal models potentially suitable for deployment, transferring across OCT datasets, devices, and clinical tasks, including three datasets not used in the student's pretraining.

AI.brief_summary: 研究视网膜 OCT 视觉基础模型的可压缩性：用 Growing Neural Gas 学习带邻接图的离散码本，将 86M 教师蒸馏为 22M 学生，并以码本为 MIM 重建目标、用图距离软交叉熵替代 one-hot 监督，在多个分类与分割基准上接近或超过教师。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「连续表示→离散码本 + 拓扑分级软监督 + 压缩后下游效用还剩多少」的设定，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态的离散化、码本式监督信号与信息保留/坍缩程度评估提供可核查线索，但任务本身与视觉推理无关。
